title: From Rs 20 a Day to Box-Office Headliner: Tamil Star Soori's Improbable Rise
excerpt: The former daily-wage worker turned comedy sidekick has delivered four consecutive Rs 50 crore-plus hits since Vetrimaaran's Viduthalai launched his reinvention.
body:
• Tamil actor Soori once earned Rs 20 a day as a daily wage worker in Tiruppur before entering the film industry in the late 1990s.
  • His 2023 breakthrough as Constable Kumaresan in Vetrimaaran's Viduthalai: Part 1 turned him from a comedy sidekick into a leading man.
  • Four consecutive films — Viduthalai Part 1, Garudan, Viduthalai Part 2, and Maaman — have each crossed Rs 50 crore at the worldwide box office.
  • His next film Mandaadi, a sports drama about a traditional fishing captain, releases on September 10.

In 1993, a young man named Ramalakshmanan Muthuchamy Thevar was working odd jobs in Tiruppur, earning Rs 20 a day. Half of his weekly Rs 140 went home to his family. A coconut bun costing Rs 1.25 was a luxury he often could not afford, settling instead for a cup of tea.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=VA-2vacOy6k

Three decades later, that same man — now known as Soori — is one of Tamil cinema's most bankable leading actors, with four consecutive films crossing the Rs 50 crore mark at the worldwide box office.

A Name Borrowed From Rajinikanth

Born in a small village, Soori was a devoted Rajinikanth fan whose admiration ran deep enough to reshape his identity. He renamed himself Surya — later shortened to Soori — after the superstar's character in Mani Ratnam's 1991 film Thalapathi, according to a report by Hindustan Times.

He entered the film industry in the late 1990s, but recognition was painfully slow. He worked as a wall painter between bit parts, taking whatever small, often uncredited roles came his way. His first real break arrived in 2009 with Vennila Kabadi Kuzhu, which earned him the nickname "Parotta" Soori. But for years afterward, he remained typecast in comic and supporting roles.

"My shirt was tossed into the costume vehicle, and I was left standing on set in just a towel wrapped around my waist, searching for my clothes while they filmed the scene with someone else. It was humiliating."

— Soori, recalling an early set experience in a Galatta interview

Vetrimaaran's Gamble That Changed Everything

The pivotal moment came in 2023, when director Vetrimaaran cast Soori as Constable Kumaresan in Viduthalai: Part 1. It was a role that demanded everything comedy did not — restraint, vulnerability, physical intensity. Soori delivered.

"Vetrimaaran sir saw something in me beyond comedy and trusted me with the role of Kumaresan," Soori told Variety India in a recent interview. "I never approached it as an opportunity to become a hero. I saw it as an opportunity to truthfully become that character."

Rajinikanth himself praised the performance publicly, calling Soori's acting "marvellous" and the film "epic." For an actor who had changed his name out of devotion to the superstar, the moment was deeply personal. "I feel my life has come full circle as the one I looked up to for entering the cinema spoke about our creation," Soori wrote on social media.

The Box-Office Streak

Viduthalai: Part 1 collected Rs 53 crore worldwide, establishing Soori as a viable lead. What followed was a streak few Tamil actors — at any stage of their careers — have managed. Garudan earned Rs 59.50 crore globally, making Soori one of the year's top Tamil draws. Viduthalai: Part 2, with Vijay Sethupathi reprising his role as rebel leader Perumal Vaathiyar, added Rs 63 crore. And Maaman, a family drama co-starring Aishwarya Lekshmi with music by Hesham Abdul Wahab, crossed Rs 50.75 crore — his fourth consecutive film to clear the Rs 50 crore line.

For an actor who spent over a decade being handed other people's shirts on set, the numbers represent something beyond commercial success. They are proof of an audience that was ready to see him differently, once a filmmaker gave them the chance.

Mandaadi and What Comes Next

Soori's next release is Mandaadi, a sports drama directed by Mathimaran Pugazhendhi that is set to open on September 10. He plays Muthukaali, a traditional fishing captain, in a film built around a coastal sport deeply rooted in Tamil culture. The film also stars Suhas and Mahima Nambiar, with music by GV Prakash.

"Being a comedian means one must understand and perform many different emotions," Soori told Variety India. "In that sense, my years in comedy prepared me well for this transition. If I give my best to the role and remain truthful to the character, the audience will automatically celebrate the hero in the film."

From Rs 20 a day to four Rs 50 crore hits in a row — Soori's trajectory is a reminder that in Indian cinema, reinvention is always possible, even when it takes three decades.
image_caption: Tamil actor Soori at a press event. Once earning Rs 20 a day, Soori has risen to become one of Tamil cinema's leading box-office draws.
nri_angle: Soori's reinvention from comedy sidekick to leading man mirrors Tamil cinema's growing reach among global diaspora audiences following regional hits.
